name: Inmolender
tagline: Spanish-market software for real estate agencies to manage properties, leads and portal listings.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The part you can see is a property database with photos, a lead inbox and some public listing pages, and an agent can build that in a weekend without breaking a sweat. The part that actually earns the subscription is the plumbing: pushing each listing out to Idealista, Fotocasa, Habitaclia and the rest in whatever XML dialect each one demands, then keeping statuses in sync when a price drops or a flat goes under contract. Those feeds need commercial portal accounts and per-portal spec compliance, not just code. If you are one agent with twenty properties and you publish manually, a self-hosted version is genuinely fine. If you are a team of six feeding five portals, you are rebuilding an integration maintenance job, not an app.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you enter properties with photos, track enquiries against them, publish public listing pages, and export a portal-style XML feed you upload yourself.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine or small VPS to run it on
Local disk or an S3-compatible bucket for property photos
Your own portal accounts if you ever want real syndication
Someone willing to read each portal's feed spec, which is the actual work
whatYouLose: Automated, maintained feeds to Idealista, Fotocasa and friends, including their periodic spec changes
Shared agency access with roles, so the office does not all use one login
Spanish legal and document boilerplate: nota de encargo, hoja de visita, GDPR consent trails
A phone-friendly app for taking photos and notes at the actual flat
Someone to call when a portal silently stops accepting your listings
moatNotes: Portal feed contracts and the migration pain of moving a few hundred live listings do more work here than any feature.
whyPeopleStillPay: Agencies do not pay for a property form, they pay for their listings appearing on the portals where Spanish buyers actually look, without anyone thinking about XML. Add the fact that the whole team, plus whoever handles paperwork, needs the same records, and that everything already lives inside it, and the calculus is boring: the subscription is cheaper than one week of someone maintaining feeds. A solo agent with a small portfolio is the real exception, and that is exactly who a self-hosted build serves.
notes: Build it if you are one agent with a spreadsheet problem, not if you are an office with a syndication problem.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted real estate listing manager for a single independent agent. Spanish-market oriented.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, SQLite via Drizzle ORM, Tailwind, server actions. No auth provider, no cloud services, no telemetry. Single-user login with one password hash read from .env.

Data model:
- Property: reference code, type (piso, casa, local, terreno), operation (venta, alquiler), price, address, municipality, province, postal code, built m2, usable m2, bedrooms, bathrooms, floor, lift, energy certificate rating, description (es), status (draft, active, reserved, sold, withdrawn), createdAt, updatedAt.
- Photo: belongs to a property, ordered, stored on local disk under /data/uploads, served through a route handler.
- Lead: name, phone, email, message, source, property it came from, status (new, contacted, viewing, offer, lost), free-text notes with timestamps.

Screens:
1. Dashboard: counts by status, leads from the last 7 days.
2. Property list with search by reference, municipality, price range and status. Bulk status change.
3. Property editor with drag-to-reorder photo upload and a live preview of the public page.
4. Lead inbox, one row per lead, inline status change and note adding.
5. Public listing pages at /inmueble/[ref] plus a public index of active properties only, server rendered, with basic Open Graph tags and a contact form that creates a Lead.

Exports:
- GET /feed.xml producing a generic property feed: one item per active property with all fields and absolute photo URLs. Document the shape in README and note clearly that real portal syndication requires each portal's own spec and a commercial account, which this does not do.
- CSV export of properties and of leads.

Rules: photos resized to max 1600px on upload with sharp, thumbnails generated. All UI strings in Spanish, prices formatted in EUR. Seed script with 8 fake properties and 5 leads. README with setup, .env.example (SESSION_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH, PUBLIC_BASE_URL), and a one-command backup that tars the SQLite file plus uploads.

Out of scope, do not build: multi-user roles, portal APIs, WhatsApp integration, contract PDF generation, mobile app.
